page: Microsoft Azure D64als_v7 is an x86_64 instance configuration in the AMD-powered Dalsv7 family, structured with a lower memory-to-vCPU allocation compared to standard general-purpose tiers. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated virtual CPUs across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Supported vector instruction extensions encompass AVX, AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16), and AVX-VNNI, alongside hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. This allocation represents a dense compute setup suited for processing tasks that do not demand extensive memory footprints. The instance includes no integrated local disk storage, depending entirely on remote Premium Storage options for operating volumes and persistent state. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this instance type.

Benchmark outcomes show high computational throughput, scoring in the top decile on the PassMark CPU suite (94,577.07) and stress-ng single-core processing (3,770.58). Memory subsystem benchmarks show uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 205.01 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 125.31 GB/sec. Data processing tasks show strong results, including top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 41.08 GB/sec and PassMark database operations at 38,333.79, accompanied by Redis write capability exceeding 103 million operations per second.

By omitting local NVMe drives and constraining memory capacity to 2.0 GB per vCPU, the D64als_v7 provides strong CPU performance per resource unit for scale-out compute footprints. It is well-aligned with distributed compute clusters, continuous integration compilation tasks, batch data transformation, CPU-based machine learning inference, and high-throughput web service environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D64als_v7 is an AMD-based compute-focused server featuring an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with multithreading, alongside 128.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Architectural support includes AVX-512 vector instruction sets and dedicated cryptographic extensions. The virtual machine does not package local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier single-core and aggregate CPU performance, alongside high data compression rates and database processing scores. With its dense core count relative to system memory, the D64als_v7 is tailored for batch processing, build automation, CPU-bound web services, and lightweight inference workloads requiring high instruction execution efficiency.
